text: Product Pricing The Vidu Open Platform provides a rich set of video generation API capabilities to meet the diverse needs of enterprises and developers. Currently, API calls are billed using a credit-based pricing model. Credit Unit Price Credits Price (RMB) 1 0.03125 Optional Top-up Package Pricing Amount (RMB) Credits Purchased Available Concurrency Validity Period 500 16,000 credits ≤ 5 1 year 1000 32,000 credits ≤ 5 1 year 2000 64,000 credits ≤ 5 1 year 5000 160,000 credits ≤ 5 1 year 20000 640,000 credits ≤ 5 1 year For business customization or bulk purchases, please contact platform@vidu.cn. We are happy to help! Notes: Videos that fail to generate do not consume credits (including failures caused by content moderation rejection). Available concurrency ≤ 5 means up to 5 concurrent tasks can be processed at the same time; additional tasks will be queued. In rare cases, system load may cause your available concurrency to fall below the maximum value. Available concurrency is unrelated to request frequency (QPS). Consumption details are as follows: Batch Size Steps Credits Required Estimated Time/Hours 4 1000 200,000 8 4 2000 400,000 14 4 3000 600,000 18 4 4000 800,000 24 8 1000 400,000 14 8 2000 800,000 24 8 3000 1,200,000 36 8 4000 1,600,000 50 For a trained fine-tuned model, each inference call consumes 40 credits. The fine-tuning feature is available by invitation only. If you need this feature, please send an email to platform@vidu.cn to apply. Recommended Prompts Billed based on the number of output prompts. For every 5 prompts output, 10 credits are deducted. Lip Sync Billed based on the duration of the lip-synced video. For every 5 seconds of video generated, 20 credits are deducted. Credit consumption for extension varies depending on the original video's resolution and model. See Q2 Pricing Information for details. Note 2: Intelligent multi-frame pricing depends on resolution and the duration of each segment. Every 2 input images form one segment; from the 2nd image to the (T-1)th image, each image serves as both the first and last frame of adjacent segments — meaning a multi-frame video can have up to 9 segments in total.
